Meeting Schedule

  1
 The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 12pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be summarized
by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City Council and will
also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be recorded for
public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials
During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items
Agenda Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7,8 ,9 and 10 are Consent Calendar Items. All items including
Ordinances, Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent
Calendar, individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion
of these items unless Members of the City Council, the public, or staff request that specific
items be removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members
of the public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three
(3) minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

  7
 Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

AP-05  Executive  Summary  - 24 CFR 91.200(c),  91.220(b)

1.  Introduction

The City of South  Gate's  2024-2025  Annual  Action  Plan (AAP) is based on priorities  established

by the City's  Five-Year  Consolidated  Plan. The 2024-2025  Action  Plan is the final  and fifth  year

of the City's  2020-2025  Consolidated  Plan.  The Five-Year  Consolidated  Plan combines  two

Federal  Department  of Housing  and Urban  Development  (HUD)  Programs  of which  the City is a

recipient  of Community  Development  Block Grant  (CDBG) and HOME  Investment  Partnerships

(HOME).

The City"s Community  Development  Department  manages,  plans,  submits,  and implements  the

CDBG and HOME grant  process.  The Department  is involved  in activities  which  enhance

coordination  among  public  and non-profit,  private  housing  providers,  and health  and service
agencies.

The 2024-2025  Annual  Action  Plan serves  as the City's  blueprint  for providing  decent  affordable

housing  to lower-income  households,  providing  suitable  living  environments,  expanding

economic  opportunities,  and expanding  the capacity  of non-profit  housing  providers  to the

residents  of South  Gate. This strategic  plan sets forth  goals,  objectives,  and performance

benchmarks  for measuring  and establishing  a framework  for progress.  The City is anticipating

receiving  91,400,000 in PY 2024-2025  CDBG funds.  The City also anticipates  receiving  S740,000
in HOME funds  for PY 2024-2025.  Currently  the City does not anticipate  any additional

carryover  funds  for programming.

  *  Promote  fair housing.

  *  Provide  infrastructure  and public  facility  funding.

  *  Provide  financial  assistance  for the rehabilitation  of commercial  faqade  improvements.

  *  Economic  Development  activities  that  promote  employment  and preserve  local

  businesses.

3.  Evaluation  of past  performance

The City continually  strives  to improve  the performance  of its operations  and those  of its

partners  who  provide  services  to City residents.  The City prepares  the Consolidated  Annual

Performance  Evaluation  and Report  (CAPER) annually,  which  documents  progress  toward

implementing  the strategies  and meeting  the goals established  in the Consolidated  Plan and the
Annual  Action  Plans.

Over the past years,  the City's  CDBG funds  were  used for meeting  the City's  goals of providing

decent  housing,  creating  a suitable  living  environment,  and expanding  economic  opportunities
to low-and  moderate-income  persons  in South  Gate.

4.  Summary  of Citizen  Participation  Process  and consultation  process

The City is committed  to maximizing  community  participation  in the CDBG and HOME  planning

process.  To ensure  that  its 2024-2025  Action  Plan was based  on resident  needs,  the City used

the following  approach  to create  participation  of residents,  service  providers,  and other

interested  persons  and organizations:

South  Gate Citizens  Advisory  Committee

The South  Gate Citizens  Advisory  Committee  (CAC) is an advisory  board  created  by the City

Council  to ensure  constant  dialog  exists  between  the City and the community.  The role of the

CAC is twofold.  First, to ensure  that  the City Council  is appraised  of the needs,  desires,  and

interests  of City residents.  Second,  to review  and make  recommendations  on CDBG funding  to

the City Council.  The CAC is comprised  of members  representing  the demographic  and social

range  of residents  in the City.  The CAC was actively  involved  in the Annual  Action  Plan process.

The CAC reviewed  and discussed  the 2024-2025  Public  Services  applications  and then  made

funding  recommendations  to the City Council  for the Annual  Action  Plan.  It is anticipated  that

the CAC will continue  to serve  in an advisory  role in the CDBG process.

AP-55  Affordable  Housing  - 91.220(g)

Introduction

One of the greatest  impediments  to affordable  housing  is the  low ratio  of available  federal  and

state  resources  to the high need of affordable  housing  needs.

As  there  are  limited  opportunities  and  funding  available  to  provide  affordable  housing

opportunities,  the  City consistently  seeks  new  partnerships  to increase  the  affordable  housing

options  in the city. Ways that  the City addressed  affordable  housing  needs  include  the following

programs:

Housing  Choice  Voucher  Program:  The  City  will  continue  to  provide  rental  assistance  to

extremely  low- and low-income  households  through  the South  Gate Housing  Authority's  Housing

Choice  Voucher  Program.  Renter-households  will  be assisted,  which  will  include  elderly,  single-
parent,  and disabled  special  needs  households.

Fair  Housing  Program:  The  City's  Fair  Housing  Program  is administered  by the  Fair  Housing

Foundation, who provide fair housing services and landlord/tenant  information  to participants
who  request  counseling,  resource  referral,  complaint  investigation,  and public  education  on all

forms  of housing  discrimination.  Renter-households  will  be assisted,  which  will  include  elderly,

single-parent,  and disabled  special  needs  households.  However,  these  are not counted  toward

the affordable  housing  goals.

Homeowner  Rehabilitation  Program:  This  program  provides  deferred  loans  to  qualified

homeowners  for rehabilitation  on their  properties.  The property  must  be brought  up to certain

housing  standards  as part of the rehabilitation  assistance.

Introduction

The City is located  within  the Los Angeles  Homeless  Services Authority  (LAHSA) Continuum.  The
continuum  provides  oversight  of federal  homeless  assistance  dollars  and collaborates  with  local
communities  to provide  the  best service  to residents  who  are homeless.  The Los Angeles
Continuum  conducts  quarterly  community  meetings,  and when appropriate  the City attends  and
participates  in  these meetings.

South  Gate  residents  who  are  of  low-to-moderate  income  and  at  risk  of  experiencing

homelessness  will  receive  assistance  to obtain  and maintain  housing  stability  through  CDBG
funded  activities.  Services  provided  may  include  income  payments  for  low-income  eligible
residents,  case management,  and referrals  for housing  support.

Describe  the jurisdiction's  one-year  goals and actions  for reducing  and ending  homelessness
including  reaching  out to homeless  persons  (especially  unsheltered  persons)  and assessing
their  individual  needs.

The Salvation  Army Bell Shelter  operates  a homeless  outreach  program  which  consists  of a
mobile  outreach  team.  In coordination  with the South Gate Police Department  Liaison and
personnel  from the Bell Shelter  street  outreach  efforts  by vehicle  and foot are undertaken.
Street  outreach,  case management,  and referrals  are provided  to homeless  families  and
individuals  through  this program.  Homeless  clients  are provided  guidance  in the identification
of barriers  to overcoming  homelessness  and the development  of a plan to address these
challenges.  The team then assists clients  at a highly supportive  level to address those needs
which  may include  accessing  mainstream  services,  increasing  income,  developing  self-
determination,  and accessing  shelter  and housing.

Addressing  the emergency  shelter  and transitional  housing  needs of homeless  persons.

Locally,  the  Salvation  Army  Bell  Shelter  operates  a comprehensive  program  that  offers
transitional  care for up to 350 homeless  men and women.  The goal of the Bell Shelter  is to meet
the needs of the homeless  population  by addressing  the myriad  of reasons why people  become
homeless  and assisting them in developing  a higher quality  oflife  through  independence.  Services
offered  include  emergency  shelter,  transitional  housing,  substance  abuse  rehabilitation,  case

management, counseling, on-site health care & medical  referrals,  HIV/AIDS education,  ESL

 classes,  computer  training,  vocational  assistance,  job  referrals  and life skills classes.

The South  Gate  Domestic  Family  Violence  Education  and Prevention  program  administered  by

the South  Gate Police  Department  provides  shelter,  court  advocacy,  counseling,  24-hour

hotline,  crisis intervention,  support  groups  and case management  to domestic  and sexual  abuse
victims.

Helping  homeless  persons  (especially  chronically  homeless  individuals  and families,  families

with  children,  veterans  and their  families,  and unaccompanied  youth)  make  the transition  to

permanent  housing  and independent  living,  including  shortening  the  period  of time  that

individuals  and families  experience  homelessness,  facilitating  access for homeless  individuals

and families  to affordable  housing  units,  and preventing  individuals  and families  who  were
recently  homeless  from  becoming  homeless  again.

The City of South  Gate collaborates  with  different  organizations  to prevent  the recurrence  of

homelessness.  The City partners  with  local organizations  and non-profits  to offer  various
programs  and resources  for residents  experiencing  homelessness  or who  are at risk of

homelessness.  Locally,  the Salvation  Army  Bell Shelter  helps address  the gaps in the City and

the need for services  to residents  experiencing  homelessness,  unemployment,  substance

abuse,  and other  social  and health  resources.  Available  services  vary from  case management,

transportation  and employment  services,  health  and mental  health  referrals,  life skills,

individual  and group  therapy,  social  and recreational  activities,  needs  assessment,  benefits

advocacy,  and permanent  housing  assistance.  The Salvation  Army  Bell Shelter  works  directly

with  the South  Gate Police  Department,  Community  Development,  Parks and Recreation,  the

Housing  Authority,  and other  local organizations  to promote  services  and reach target
populations.

To help prevent  the recurrence  of homelessness  the program  helps  participants  search  for

permanent  housing  and seek employment  to maintain  their  home.  Their  case management

team  conducts  workshops  to assist residents  with  building  resumes  and career  prep.

Participants  are referred  to job openings  and job fairs and are encouraged  to participate  in

extracurricular  activities  such as attending  monthly  meetings,  events,  and volunteering  at the
community  garden.

To combat  homelessness,  the City funds  a comprehensive  Fair Housing  Program  that  offers

education  and outreach  activities  for tenants,  landlords,  and owners.  Education  consists  of

workshops,  presentations,  community  meetings,  and training.  The purpose  of this program  is to

guide  all parties  on their  rights,  laws, and responsibilities.  The Fair Housing  Program  conducts

Helping  low-income  individuals  and families  avoid  becoming  homeless,  especially  extremely

low-income  individuals  and families  and those  who  are: being  discharged  from  publicly

funded  institutions  and systems  of care (such  as health  care facilities,  mental  health  facilities,

foster  care and other  youth  facilities,  and corrections  programs  and institutions);  or, receiving

assistance  from  public  or private  agencies  that  address  housing,  health,  social  services,
employment,  education,  or youth  needs.

The South  Gate Police  Department  has different  practice  methods  for individuals  being

discharged  and who  are seeking  support  services.  The Police  Department  links individuals  to

available  resources  and agencies  in the City including  People  Assisting  the Homeless  (PATH),

which  is an organization  that  helps  individuals  experiencing  homelessness  in their  community.

PATH distributes  food,  and clothing  to residents,  connects  residents  to permanent  housing,  and
provides  ongoing  supportive  services  for residents  in need.  PATH has an outreach  and

prevention  team  that  works  in areas where  homelessness  is more  prevalent  and connects

individuals  with  employment.  The South  Gate Police  Department  refers  individuals  who  are

being  discharged  from  jail to PATH for interim  housing,  rapid  rehousing,  employment,  and
other  permanent  supportive  services.

There  are no hospitals  in the City of South  Gate,  therefore  the City does not often  have

individuals  who  are being  discharged  from  hospitals.  However,  if individuals  are seeking

information  the Police  Department  reaches  out to PATH staff  for resources,  and supportive

 AP-75  Barriers  to  affordable  housing  - 91.220(j)

Introduction:

The impact  on housing  affordability  disproportionately  affects  those  who are lower  income.  HUD

considers  a housing  unit affordable  if the occupant  household  expends  no more  than  30% of its

income  on housing  cost.  In the situation  where  the household  expends  greater  than  30% of its

income  on housing  cost, the  household  is considered  cost burdened.  Cost burdened  households

have fewer  financial  resources  to meet  other  basic needs (food,  clothing,  transportation,  medical,

etc.),  less  resources  to  properly  maintain  the  housing  structure,  and  are  at greater  risk for
foreclosure  or eviction.

Recent  sales data for South  Gate shows  that  housing  prices  continue  to increase,  while  household

incomes  have  failed  to keep  pace  with  home  prices.  There  are also other  factors  that  create

barriers  to affordable  housing  growth.  The  barriers  that  typically  affect  housing  costs  are as
follows:

  *  Lack of developable  land and/or where  development  is due to zoning.

  *  Cost of developable  land and construction.

  *  Credit  worthiness  of potential  buyers  for homeownership.

  *  Social opinions  discouraging  affordable  development  in particular  neighborhoods  (Not in

  My Backyard  "NIMBY").

  *  Lack of responsible  landlords  for maintaining  safe and clean-living  conditions.

  *  Credit  worthiness  of potential  renters.

Actions  it planned  to remove  or ameliorate  the negative  effects  of public  policies  that  serve

as barriers  to affordable  housing  such as land  use controls,  tax policies  affecting  land,  zoning

ordinances,  building  codes,  fees and charges,  growth  limitations,  and policies  affecting  the
return  on residential  investment.

The City adopted  General  Plan 2035  in 2009.  As part of the General  Plan update,  a new concept

in dealing  with  land use and development  standards  was introduced.  Unlike  traditional  Euclidean

land use and zoning  system,  the proposed  South  Gate General  Plan uses a "form  based"  system
to determine  location  and intensity  of uses.

The  new  Zoning  Ordinance  update  was  adopted  in March  2015.  The  City's  current  estimated

number  of dwelling  units  is about  24,242  units.  The  Zoning  Update  has created  density  and

Actions  planned  to address  obstacles  to meeting  underserved  needs.

The primary  obstacles  to meeting  the  underserved  needs  of low-and  moderate-income  people

include  lack of funding  from  federal,  state,  and other  local sources,  the high cost of housing  that

is not  affordable  to  low-and  moderate-income  people  and  the  lack  of  availability  of  home

improvement  financing  in the  private  lending  industry.  To address  these  obstacles,  the  City  is

investing  HOME funds  towards  the construction  of affordable  housing  development.  CDBG funds

are being  allocated  to organizations  that  provide  public  and neighborhood  services  to low-and

moderate-income  people  and those  with  special  needs that  can help offset  other  household  costs

that  create  financial  burdens  for individuals.

Choice Voucher  Program  to very low-income  households  through  its Housing  Authority.  The City

certifies  Community  Housing  Development  Organizations  (CHDOs)  to provide  affordable  housing

Actions  planned  to reduce  lead-based  paint  hazards.

All units in a project  assisted with CDBG and HOME funds must comply  with the regulations  found
at 24 CFR Part 35.  The purpose  of the regulation  is to identify  and address  lead-based  paint
hazards  before  children  are  exposed  to  lead.  This  requirement  has been  in effect  since
September  15, 2000.

Lead-based  paint  hazards are found  in homes built prior to 1978.  All Grantees  and Participating
Jurisdictions  must  assess homes  built  prior  to 1978  for lead hazards  and conduct  interim  or
abatement  controls  as warranted.  Most of the homes in South Gate were built prior to 1978  and
have lead-based  paint somewhere  on the structure.  Lead based paint  is found  on windowsills,
doorways  or under  the eaves.  The hazards  of lead-based  paint  are primarily  to young  children
uptoage6,astheyaremorelikelytoeatpeelingpaint.  Leadadverselyaffectsthedevelopment
of a child's  brain and other  organs.

The City's strategy  in addressing  lead-based  paint  hazards  involves  an educational  component
for the  public,  printed  outreach  information  to those  households  in the "lead  hot zones"  as
identified  by the  County,  and  printed  information  are given  to  participants  in the  City's
rehabilitation  loan programs.

The City offers  a Residential  Rehabilitation  Program  which  focuses  on rehabilitating  existing

housing stock throughout  the City covering interior and exterior home improvement and/or
repairs. In combination with the Residential Rehabilitation  Program,  the City offers  SI0,000
grants  to be used for termite  and lead abatement.  Lead assessments  are conducted  on all
housing  projects,  both single family  and multi-family  units. All HCV participant  rental  units are
inspected  annually.

 SUBJECT:  ORDINANCE  N0.  2024-01-CC  INCREASING  CITY  COUNCIL  AND  CITY
 TRE,ASURER  SALARY  LF,VELS

 PURPOSE:  To consider  adopting  Ordinance  No. 2024-01-CC  amending  the City  Council  and
 the City  Treasurer  salary  levels.

 RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider  adopting  Ordinance  No. 2024-
 01-CC  amending  Section  1.04.065.2  (Same  - Compensation)  of Section  1.04.065  (Salaiy  Of
 Members  - Purpose)  of Chapter  1.04 (City  Council)  of Title  l (Administration  And  Personnel)  of
 the South  Gate Municipal  Code increasing  the City  Council  and the City  Treasurer  salai'y levels.

 FISCAL  IMPACT:  The  salary  change  recommended  is proposed  to  become  effective  in
 December  2024.  If enacted  as proposed,  the City  Corincil  monthly  salaiy  would  increase  from
 $790  to $1,900  per  month  resulting  in  an increase  to the  current  City  Council's  combined
 compensation  of $5,550  for all 'five members.  In addition,  the City Treasurer's  salaiy  is tied to that
 of the City  Council  per Section  1.05.065  (City  Treasurer  - Compensation)  which  voters  approved
 in November  2000,  this change  worild  result  in a monthly  increase  for the Treasurer  of $1,110.
 There will  be no fiscal  impact  due to this change  for the FY2023-24  budget  as the change  is not to
 stait until  December  of 2024.  The budget  proposal  for FY2024-25  will  include  a funding  request
 to cover this increase  for the coming  fiscal  year.

 ANALYSIS:  Senate  Bill  329 took  effect  on January  1, 2024,  and provides  new pay caps for
 California  City  Council  members  based on City  population  size. The City  Council  discussed  the
 new $1,900  monthly  cap and directed  staff to take action  to make a change  in their pay to this new
 level. The City  Council  determined  that moving  the City  Council  and City  Treasurer  monthly  pay
 to the cap would  be a fair  level  of compensation  for work  expected  and would  provide  a better
 financial  incentive  for new individuals  to run for City  elected  positions  in the future.

 BACKGROUND:  At  the March  26, 2024  City  Council  Meeting,  the City  Council  received
 information  to consider  approving  a proposed  ordinance  amending  the City  Council  and the City
 Treasrirer's  salary  levels.  At the January  9, 2024 City Council  meeting,  the City  Corincil  requested
 a report  on the newly  passed Senate Bill  329 legislation  that sets new City  Council  pay caps. This
 new legislation  was presented  for discussion  at the March  12, 2024,  City  Council  meeting.  The

  I

  64
 new law took effect  January  1, 2024,  and was authored  by Senator  Bill  Dodd.  His explanation  for
supporting  increased  pay levels  for City  Council  members  was, "No  one runs for city  council  to
get rich. But the low levels  of pay make it much harder  to balance  careers and personal  obligations
with  the call to serve their  community."  He went  on to say, "It  is especially  hard for working
people  and those from  diverse  or disadvantaged  backgrounds.  By allowing  councils  to adjust  their
maximum  pay  to reflect  inflation,  my  bill  will  remove  barriers  to achieving  more  equitable
representation  in local govennment."

The new law is now a part of Califotania  Goveinment  Code 36516  which  is attached  to this repoit.
The new caps range from  $950 per month  for cities  with  up to 35,000  in population,  to $3,200  per
month  for cities  with  populations  over 250,000.  The cap provided  for a city the size of South  Gate
(approximately  100,000  population),  is $1,900  per month  which  covers  cities  with  populations
between  75,000  and 150,000.

The current  pay rate for South Gate Corincil  members  is $790 per montli.  A rate of $600 per month
was established  in 1986 and changed  to $650 per month  in 2017. The rate was increased  to $790
per month  in 2022.  The City  Treasurer  receives  the same monthly  amount  as the City  Council
members.

At the March  12, 2024 City Council  meeting,  the City Council  directed  staff to pursue the adoption
of an ordinance  to increase  the compensation  for the City  Council  members  and City  Treasurer  to
the new cap limit  of $1,900  per month.  In order  to enact this change,  the new law provides  the
following  guidance:

Section  36516  - 4 (G)
(l)  For the purposes  of this section,  a city  corincil  shall consider  the adoption  of an ordinance  to
increase  compensation  in open session  during  at least two regular  meetings  of the city corincil.
(2) At the first meeting,  the city corincil  shall present  the proposed  ordinance,  which  shall include
findings  demonstrating  the need  for  the  increased  compensation.  The  ordinance  shall  not  be
adopted  at the first meeting.
(3) At  least seven  days after  the first  meeting,  the city  council  shall  hold  a second  meeting  to
consider  whether  to adopt the ordinance.

At the March  26, 2024 City  Council  Meeting,  the City  Council  approved  the proposed  ordinance
and directed  staff to bring  the ordinance  back for final  approval  at the April  9, 2024 City  Council
meeting.  A proposed  Ordinance  is attached  to this repoit  and includes  findings  demonstrating  the
need for increased  compensation.

BACKGROUND:  The Project is a part of the FY 2022/23 Capital Improvement Program.  The
Project is located between the Los Angeles River, Firestone Boulevard, the Thunderbird Villa
Mobile Home Park, and the I-710 Freeway. The two primary purposes of the Project are to divert
and treat stori'n water run-off from the Los Angeles River and to install a new park to provide
riverfront  recreational  opportunities.

by an entity known as Southeastern Disposal and By-Products. The property site is identified in
CalRecycle's Solid Waste Information System ("SWIS") as an Unpermitted Closed Solid Waste
Disposal Site and SWIS No. 19-AA-5545. In 1984, the State of California Department of Health

working  with  the LEA  to obtain  approval  of the PCLUP.

  PURPOSE:  To ten'ninate  Contract  No. 2022-84-CC  ("Agreement")  between  the City  of South
  Gate and NR Development,  Inc. ("NR  Development")  for default  per Section  6-7 ("Teri'nination
  of the Contract  for Default")  of the 2021  Standard  Specifications  for Public  Works  Construction
  ("Greenbook")  for the construction  of the Hollydale  Community  Park Project,  City  Project  No.
  607-PRK  ("Project"),  effective  April  9, 2024.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Adopting  a Resolution  to terminate  Contract  No. 2022-84-CC  between  the City  of South
  Gate and NR  Development,  Inc.,  for default  effective  April  9, 2024,  for the Hollydale
  Cornrnunity  Park Project,  City  Project  No. 607-PRK;
  b.  Directing  the Mayor  to execute  a document  in a fori'n  acceptable  to the City  Attorney
  advising  NR Development,  Inc.,  and the bonding  company  that the Agreement  has been
  ten'ninated  for default;  and
  c.  Authorizing  tlie City  Manager,  or his designee,  to execute  any related  documentation  in
  pursuit  of the City's  remedies  against  NR Development,  including  its bonding  company  in
  an effort  to complete  the Project  including,  but not limited  to, the retention  of a successor
  contractor.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There is no impact  to the General  Fund. Termination  of the Agreement  will
  not require  the City  to compensate  NR Development,  Inc. since they have been compensated  for
  work  completed  to date.  Since  the City  has declared  the contractor  to be in default  under  its
  Agreement  for the Project,  the City  has the right  to charge  NR Development  liquidated  damages
  starting  October  27, 2023, at an amount  of $1,000  per working  day as stipulated  in the Agreement
  documents  which  amount  to $118,000  as of April  9, 2024.  The Project  has received  a total  of
  $6,043,452  in grant  fimds,  of which  approximately  $1,707,904  (about  34%) remain  available,  be
  utilized  to fund  Project  costs  associated  with  terminating  the Agreement  and completing  the
  construction  of the Project  under  a new agreement.

 ANALYSIS:  OnSeptember27,2021,tlieCityCouncilapprovedContractNo.2022-84-CCwith
NR  Development  in the amount  of $4,899,816  for the construction  of the Project.  The  initial
approved  construction  scl'iedule  required  construction  to begin  on November  2, 2022  and to be
completed  by  September  5, 2023.  Unfortunately,  NR  Development  was unable  to complete
construction  and has abandoned  tlie job site.

Section  6-7 of the Greenbook  peri'nits  the City  to terminate  the Agreement  wlien  the contractor
fails  to cure  a default  related  to the  contractor's  obligations.  Section  6-7  specifies  general
categories  of default,  provides  for specified  notices  to be delivered  by the City  and sets forth
obligations  of the surety.  As reflected  below,  City  staff complied  with  the requisite  notices  setting
forth  the nature  of default  by NR Development,  and its subsequent  failure  to cure.

Accordingly,  City  staff recommends  the City  Council  declare  NR Development  to be in default
under  its Agreement  for the Project  and to exercise  appropriate  remedies,  which  includes  making
a claim  under the performance  bond provided  to the City by NR Development  in coru'iection  with
the Project.  City  staff took reasonable  steps in compliance  with  Section  6-7 in advance  of making
this recoinmendation.

  @  On October  11, 2023,  the City  stated its concern  regarding  the prosecution  of work  on the
  Project,  because the completion  deadline  of October  26, 2023, was only two weeks  away.

  The City  requested  a recovery  schedule  from  NR Development.  NR Development  never

  provided  the City  with  the recovery  schedule.

  *  On October  19, 2023,  the City  emailed  the Notice  to Cure letter  to NR Development  to
  prosecute  the work  in a timely  manner.  NR  Development  initially  complied  with  the
  request  prosecuted  work  at an acceptable  level  for  an estimated  two  to three  weeks.
  Thereafter,  their perfonnance  declined  dramatically.

  *  On December  12, 2023, the City  submitted  a Notice  of Liquidated  Damages  notifying  NR
  Development  that it had accrued  30 days in Liquidated  Damages.

  *  On January  5, 2024, NR Development  submitted  a letter to the City coinmitting  to finishing
  the remaining  work  on the Project.

  *  On January  15, 2024,  and for the next six consecutive  working  days, the City witnessed  no
  activity  on the Project  site. However,  on January  23, 2024, the City visited  the job site and
  found  that NR Development  sent one laborer  to install  sections  of the irrigation  line  for a
  few hours.  There  was no further  activity  on site thereafter.

  *  InspiteofNRDevelopment'scommitmenttocompletetheProject,theCityhadwitnessed
  a very low level of production  and for the last 16 consecutive  working  days. There  was no
  activity  on the job site from  January  24 to February  14, 2024.

  *  On February  14, 2024,  the City  notified  NR Development  that it had incurred  80 working
  days  of  Liquidated  Damages  owing  to the  City,  and  it must  complete  all  remaining
  improvements  per Agreement  documents  and as directed  by the City Engineer  no later than
  March  29, 2024.

   *  NR Development  failed  to meet the March  29f" deadline.  As of March  29, 2024,  the City
  had not seen any construction  activity  on the Project  site since January  24, 2024.  It is
  apparent  to the City  that NR Development  did not make any effort  to meet this deadline.

Despite  repeated  requests  from  the City to NR Development  to continue  progressing  on the work
for the Project  in a diligent  and acceptable  manner,  NR Development  has failed  to do so. It has not
made a good faith  effort  to provide  sufficient  resources  to finalize  the remaining  scope of work  in

a timely  manner.  This  noncompliance  has resulted  in substantial  financial  damages  to the City
due to the delay.  The  City  is suspending  construction  activities  at the Project  site after  NR
Development  has failed  to fulfil  its contractual  obligations,  comply  with  Plans and Specifications,
and has not performed  any construction  on the Project  witliin  the last 11 weeks.

The accrual  of additional  financial  damages  can be minimized  by teri'ninating  Contract  No. 2022-
84-CC  as soon  as possible  and resuming  the Project  under  a new  construction  agreement  in
coordination  with  the bonding  company.  As such, City staff recommends  the City  Council  declare
the contractor  to be in default  under  its Agreement  for the Project.

BACKGROUND:  The  Project  is  budgeted  in  the  Capital  Improvement  Program.  The
improvements  proposed  include  a 1,700  square-foot  building,  storm  water chambers,  playground,
synthetic  turf, sand and water play area, basketball  court shade structures,  a new irrigation  system,
decomposed  granite,  park bench  and picnic  tables, permeable  pavers,  concrete  flat work,  and other
miscellaneous  park  amenities.  The  construction  on  the  Project  is  currently  at  about  80%
completion.

NR  Development  was  awarded  a construction  Agreement  to  complete  the  Project  and has
abandoned  the job site.  It is estimated  that NR Development  completed  80% or less of the required
Agi-eement  work  before  abandoning  the Project.

It is uncertain  how  long  it will  take to complete  construction  of the Project.  The  City  will  be
discussing  with  the bonding  company  to  outline  the  process  and  schedule  for  construction
completion.

   INDEMNIFICATION  AND  LIABILITY  INSURANCE  REQUIREMENTS

The following  requirements  must  be met when  submitting  insurance  certificates  to the City  of
South Gate in connection  with  Public  Works  and other projects:

  The insurance  certificate  must be issuedto  the City of South Gate, 8650 California  Avenue,
  South Gate, CA  90280,  attention  of the City Engineer.

  The City  of South  Gate,  South  Gate Housing  Authority,  and their  officers,  employees,
  elected  officials,  and agents must be shown  as additional  insured  per ISO CG 20 101185,
  and separate endorsement  signed by an a'uthorized  representative  ofthe  insurance  company
  is required.

  The  City  has the right  to request  a copy  of complete  insurance  policy  including  all
  endorsements  and certificates.

  The Certificate  must  include  cross liability  coverage  either  included  in the Commercial
  General  Liability  coverage,  and so indicate  on the face ofthe  Certificate  underthat  heading
  or by separate endorsement.

  The Certificate  should  also indicate  that the insurance  covers "All  Operations"  or should
  specify  the particular  services  to be provided.

  Contractor  shall procure  and maintain  for the duration  of the Contract  insurance  against
  claims  for injuries  to persons ordamages  to property  whichmay  arise from or in connection
  with the performance  of the work  hereunder  by the Contractor,  his agents, representatives,
  employees  or subcontractors.

  Minimum  Scope of Insurance

  Coverage  shall be at least as broad as:

  1.  Insurance  Services  Office  Commercial  General  Liability  coverage  (occurrence
  from CG 0001).

  2.  Insurance  Services  Office  form  number  CA 0001 (Ed. 1/87)  covering  Automobile
  Liability,  code 1 (any auto).

  3.  Workers'  Compensation  insurance  as required  by  the  State  of  California  and
  Employer's  Liability  Insurance.

  4.  Course  of Construction  insurance  covering  for "all  risks"  of loss.  Earthquake  and
  flood  insurance  is not required  to be furnished  by the Contractor

 Contractor  shall maintain  limits  no less than:

1.  General  Liability:  $1,000,000  per occurrence  for bodily  injury,  personal  injury  and

  general  aggregate  limit  is used,  either  the general  aggregate  limit  shall  apply

  damage.

the Contractor  shall  provide  a financial  guarantee  satisfactory  to the City  guaranteeing
payment  of losses and related  investigations,  claim  administration  and defense expenses.

  materials,  parts or equipment  furnished  in connection  with  suchwork  or operations.

  Contractor's  insurance  or as a separate owner's  policy.

  maintained  by the City,  its officers,  officials,  employees,  or volunteers  shall  be

3.  Each insurance  policy  required  by this clause  shall be endorsed  to state that coverage

  PURPOSE:  To approve  Amendment  No. 1 to Contract  No. 2023-24-CC  with  Gannett  Fleming,
  Inc.,  ("Garu'iett  Flemming")  for additional  Construction  Management  and Inspection  Services  for
  the Garfield  Avenue  Complete  Street  Improvement  Project,  City  Project  No.  564-ST  ("Project")
  through  construction  completion  scheduled  for April  2024.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Amendment  No. 1 to Contract  No. 2023-24-CC  with  Gannett  Fleming,  Inc., to
  provide  additional  construction  management  and inspection  services  for the construction
  of the Garfield  Avenue  Complete  Street Improvement  Project,  City Project  No. 564-ST,  at
  a cost not to exceed $144,067;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  Amendment  No.  1 in a fori'n  acceptable  to the City
  Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact  to the General  Fund.  The proposed  Agreement  is
  in the amount  of $144,067  and it will  be funded  with  Road Mitigation  Fee Funds budgeted  in the
  Fiscal  Year  2023/24  Capital  Improvement  Program.  The revised  contract  amount  is $505,925,
  inclusive  of  Contract  No.  2023-24-CC  and Amendment  No.  1.  The  total  project  budget  is
  $6,551,700  which  is funded  withRoadMitigationFee  Funds ($1M),  MeasureW,  ($600,000),  TDA
  Fund ($195,000)  Prop C Funds ($1,520,000),  Measure  M Funds  ($700,000)  and Measure  M Local
  Match  Funds  ($337,070),  Federal  Funds  ($1,539,630)  and State Funds  ($660,000).

  ANALYSIS:  The construction  of the Project  is in progress.  Under  Contract  No.  2023-24-CC,
  Gannett  Fleming  is providing  construction  management  and inspection  services  for  a 140-day
  construction  schedule.  A contract  amendment  is needed  to fund  55 working  days of additional
  costs and services,  for a total construction  schedule  of 195 working  days.  The schedule  extension
  was warranted  due to unforeseen  issues that were encountered  during  construction.  This included
  (a) design  changes  to grade  elevations  and curb  extension  construction,  (b) construction  delays
  related  to the SCE service  request  schedule,  and (c) obtaining  Right  of Entry  and coordinating  the

  152
 work with Union Pacific Railroad at Garfield Avenue and Imperial Highway.

Amendment No. l to Contract No. 2023-24-CC provides $144,067 to cover the additional  55
working days of services. Services needed include administration,  construction management,
inspection, labor compliance, materials testing and utility coordination through construction
completion  in April 2024.

BACKGROUND:  The Project is budgeted in the FY 2023/24 CIP. Improvements are plaru'ied
from Firestone Boulevard to Jefferson Avenue. The improvements include bike lanes on Garfield
Avenue from Firestone Boulevard to Harding Avenue, on Gardendale Street from Garfield Avenue
to the Los Angeles River, and on Frontage Road Miller Way and Southern Avenue west of Garfield
to their respective teiminations.  The improvements  on Garfield Avenue also include  raised
landscape medians with a new irrigation system, drought tolerant landscaping, traffic calming
measures, sidewalk and ADA improvements,  traffic signing and striping, and storm water
mitigations.  Enhanced pedestrian crosswalks with rapid flashing beacons will be installed at
Garfield Avenue just north of Southern Avenue, Garfield Avenue at Roosevelt Avenue  and
Garfield  Avenue  at Harding  Avenue.

On March 14, 2023, the City Council approved Contract No. 2023-24-CC with Gannett Fleming
for construction management and inspection services in the amount of $361,858, which reflected
a construction schedule of 140 working days. After construction management services began,
additional costs were incurred for related, but out of scope work, that were paid from the original
contract  amount  as summarized  below.

  *  A total of $21,857 for additional work was authorized which included time and material
  supervision of bulb-out corner construction, relocation of traffic signal conduits, project
  construction signs and other contractor supervision services.

  *  Construction of the Project was stopped from December 6, 2023, to February 12, 2024.
  The construction stoppage was necessary due to delays related to obtaining service from
  Southern California Edison (SCE) for the new irrigation system controllers, coordination
  with UPRR for the crossing at Imperial Highway, and issues with the constructability  of
  street bulb-outs. During this time, Gannett Fleming incurred $3,597 in delay costs.

Construction  began on May 2023 and is scheduled for completion  in April  2024.

  SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH  SDI  PRESENCE  LLC  FOR  SUPPLEMENT  AL  IT
  SUPPORT  SERVICES

  PURPOSE:  To approve an Agreement with SDI Presence LLC,  a managed  service provider  for
  supplemental  IT staffing and project-related tasks.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  an agreement  with  SDI Presence  LLC.,  to provide  on-site  Supplemental  IT
  support,  for one year, in the amount of $104,858;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute the Agreement  in a form acceptable  to tlie City Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  No impact.  The funds were appropriated  in the FY 2023-24  Budget.

  ALIGNMENT  WITH  COUNCIL  GOALS:  On January 28, 2020, Council  accepted the City's
  Technology  Master Plan ("TMP")  prepared by ClientFirst  Technology  Consulting  ("ClientFirst").
  The TMP  includes  an assortment  of projects  to improve  the City's  network  infrasttucture  and
  servtces.

  Examples  of approved  TMP  projects:
  *  Network  and wireless  equipment  upgrades
  *  Servers and storage area network  ("SAN")  infrastructure  upgrades
  @  Cybersecurity  improvements
  *  IT operational  improvements  for CIS Division  efficiencies

  ANALYSIS:
  Current  IT  staffing  levels  are insufficient  to support  the number  of day-to-day  requests  and
  ongoing  or upcoming  project-related  infrastructure  and resource  improvements.  This  staffing
  shortfall causes an increase in overtime  for existing  IT staff and delays the completion  of projects
  and tasks.

 Since  the adoption  of the 2020  TMP,  numerous  projects  have been impacted  because  of staff
sl'iortages.  Below  are examples  of projects  that exceeded  their schedules:
  *  Phone  System  Upgrade
  *  Active  Directory  (AD)  Clean  Up
  @  Core Network  Upgrade
  *  Patch management  solution
  @  Computer  upgrades
  *  City  Hall  Servers  and SAN  replacement/upgrade
  *  Microsoft  365 (M365)  Cloud  integration  for home  directories  and shared files
  *  Mobile  Device  Management  (MDM)
  *  Multifactor  Authentication  (MFA)
  @  Expansion  of wireless  (Wi-Fi)  across all departments  and sites

As of March  4, 2024,  of this fiscal  year, IT staff accumulated  approximately  $22,655  in overtime.
It should  be noted that tliis additional  approved  overtime  has been insufficient  to keep projects  and
tasks on track.

In surnrnary,  approval  of this request  will  improve  service  quality  and response  times  for the user
community  and aid in tlie completion  of critical  infrastructure  projects.  Supplemental  IT services
will  help Council-approved  projects  to finish  on time and within  budget,  while  also balancing  staff
workloads  and reducing  staff burnout.

BACKGROUND:  Before,  during,  and after the Covid-19  pandemic,  limited  staff availability
resulted  in budge-t  r-ev-i-sions, delays  of day-to-day  operations,  and technical  issues  because  of
outdated  systems  and  limited  resources.  Furthermore,  previously  approved  projects  were
significantly  impacted  by the global  microchip  supply  chain shortage.

ClientFirst  worked  with  City  IT staff to develop  and release  an RFP for Supplemental  IT Support
Services.  The RFP was released  on September  7, 2023.  Tlie City  received  a total  of four vendor
proposals  and then selected  the two  lowest  cost proposals  as finalists.  Staff  worked  with  the two
finalist  vendors  (SDI  Presence  LLC "SDI"  and Kapital  Date Corp "Kapital")  to validate  alignment
with  tlie RFP and the needs of the City.  Tlie RFP stated that the City  is seeking  a managed  service
provider  for one year of on-site  Supplemental  IT Support  Services  (20 hours  per week).

Virtualization
SDI is an advocate  of virtualization.  The benefits  ofvirtualization  are significant  and continuously  evolving.
Immediate  benefits  support  data center  modernization  while  extended  benefits  result  in lessened  capital
expenditures  and an overall  reduction  in the total  cost of ownership.  Transitioning  from  a physical  server
model,  where  physical  servers  often  perform  individual  tasks and underutilize  resources,  to a virtualized
model,  where  physical  servers  host many virtual  servers  and optimize  resource  utilization  is the first  and
most  apparent  benefit.  However,  virtualization  also provides  added  flexibility  and scalability  by pooling
resources  for computing,  storage,  and networking  permits  load balancing,  and simplifies  disaster  recovery
procedures.

Relevant  to the  City of South  Gate's  virtualized  environment,  SDl"s typical  design,  configuration,  and
management  of the  virtualized  environments  at nearly  all Los Angeles  and Orange  County  municipal
clients include multi-host,  high-availability clusters operating  on vCenter/vSphere  6.5-7.0
Standard/Essentials Plus with managed or standalone  ESXi 6.x-7.x VMware  hosts. Storage integration  is
ideally  iSCSl connected  flash array(s)  that support  compression,  deduplication,  and immutable  snapshots.
Alternate  configurations  may employ  iSCSl connected  SAN or on-board  storage.  SDI's scope  of services
include the full spectrum  of initial design and setup, physical-to-virtual conversion/migration,  storage
integration/replacement,  platform modernization,  and daily management and maintenance.  SDI also
supports  Microsoft  Hyper-V  environments  on a variety  of current  operating  system  and storage  platforms.

Disaster  Recovery
SDI designs,  deploys,  and supports  various  systems  that  leverage  technologies  labeled  as high availability,
clustered,  fault  tolerant,  redundant,  and others,  but even the  most  robust  of systems  may occasionally
experience  an event  that  affects  the availability  of data.  To mitigate  the risk of such an event  adversely
affecting  the continuity  of operations,  SDI employs  a layered  disaster  recovery  model  that  leverages  a
combination  of available  solutions  including  SAN snapshots,  on-site  backup  repositories,  off-site  backup
repositories, and may even resort to seeminBly  legacy offline tape backcip repositories to ensure a client's
data is protected  and available  for restoration  in the event  of a disaster.

  PURPOSE:  To  approve  an  Agreement  with  Macro  Automatics  ("Agreement")  for  the
  implementation  of the Supervisory  Control  and Data Acquisition  System  Upgrade,  City  Project
  No. 647-WTR  ("SCADA  Project").

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  an Agreement  with  Macro  Automatics  for Professional  Engineering  Services
  to implement  the Supervisory  Control  and Data Acquisition  System  Upgrade,  City  Project
  No. 647-WTR,  in an amount  not to exceed  $539,882;

  to fully  fund the SCADA  Project;  and
  c.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute tlie Agreement  in a form acceptable  to the City Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The proposed  Agreement  is in the
  amount  of $539,882  and is proposed  to be funded  with  Water  Funds.  The  SCADA  Project  is
  budgeted  in the amount  of $500,000  in Water  Funds.  The proposed  budget  is $725,000  which
  requires  an appropriation  in the amount  of $225,000  in Water  Funds.  The budget  is planned  to be
  utilized  as summarized  below.

  ANALYSIS:  On July  11, 2023,  the City  Council  approved  Contract  No.  2023-96-CC  with
  HydroScientific  West  for the implementation  of the SCADA  Project  in the amount  of $597,621.
  Since the award  of the contract,  HydroScientific  West has been unable  to perform  the work  due to
  the owner/operator  being  diagnosed  with  major  health  issues  and ultimately  succumbing  to the

  I

  238
 illness  in December  2023.  The  owner/operator  was the sole  employee  of the company,  thus
HydroScientific  West will  not be able perform  the work.  As such, the contract  between  the City
of South Gate and HydroScientific  West is being  terminated.

Staff is recommending  proceeding  to award  the contract  to Macro  Automatics,  the second highest
ranked  consultant  during  the initial  RFP  process.  Macro  Automatics  was  able to honor  their
original  fee proposal;  however,  a couple  of changes  were  made  which  are not  an issue.  The
materials  and labor  cost increased,  but Macro  Automatics  was able to offset  those increased  costs
by  reducing  the  as-needed  maintenance  cost  and  the  additional  cost  category.  As-needed
maintenance  services  for a 3-year  period  was reduced  from  $90,000  to $80,000.  This  decreased
amount  is not an issue since the Supervisory  Control  and Data Acquisition  ("SCADA")  system
will  be new. Also,  reducing  the as-need maintenance  cost by $3,300  per year will  likely  not impact
SCADA  maintenance.  The additional  cost category  covers  the cost of the professional  liability
insurance  where  coverage  was reduced  from  $5 million  to $1 million,  which  is within  the limits  of
our standard  professional  services  agreement.

The RFP requested  services  based on three tasks:  Task A was for Non-optional  Work  Items;  Task
B  was  for  Optional  Work  Items;  and  Task  C was  for  Operations  and  Maintenance.  Staff
recommends  awarding  a contract  to  Macro  Automatics  for  all  three  tasks  because  it  will
significantly  improve  system reliability  at the South Gate Park facility  by, (a) adding  an extra PLC,
(b) eliminating  the old signal wiring  system,  and (c) adding  new equipment  such as computers  that
are compatible  with  the new system.  The Agreement  also includes  a 3-year  period  of as-needed
SCADA  system  maintenance  and operations,  troubleshooting  and technical  support,  resetting
alarm  signals,  integration  of new equipment/processors,  minor  repairs,  and other additional  tasks.

The proposed  term  of the agreement  is four  (4) years which  provides  time  for installation  of the
new SCADA  system  and three (3) years of maintenance.

BACKGROUND:  The  City's  municipal  water  system  is a complex  network  of  facilities
consisting  of ten water  wells,  four booster  pump  stations,  four reservoir  sites, and over 135 miles
of water  distribution  pipelines  (Attachment  B - Water  System  Map).  One of the tools  utilized  to

  2

  239
 manage  and operate  the water  system's  facilities  is la'iown  as the SCADA  system.  The SCADA
system  is a so'ftware  and hardware  program  that provides  the ability  to operate  water  facilities
remotely,  in real-time,  from  a central  computer  station  located  at the City's  Corporate  Yard.
SCADA  software  and hardware  is installed  at the location  of several  water  facilities.  The SCADA
system  is a vital  component  of the water  system.  The existing  SCADA  has been in place  since
2013  and the current  software/hardware  in use is obsolete  and does not provide  adequate  cyber
security.  Therefore,  the system  is recorni'nended  for replacement.

The SCADA  Project  is budgeted  in the FY 2023/24  Capital  Improvement  Program  to replace  and
upgrade  the existing  SCADA  system.  The  SCADA  project  will  provide  the components  and
programining  for upgrading  the system  with  a new, fully  functioning  SCADA  system.

An  Agreement  is proposed  to be awarded  to Macro  Automatics.  The Agreement  provides  for
removing  the existing  SCADA  system  and installing  a new one. Macro  Automatics  provides  a
wealth  of experience  in replacing  and transitioning  the old  SCADA  system  to the proposed
SCADA  system.  They have the experience  needed to methodically  upgrade  the outdated  hardware
with  minimal  downtime.  They  have  successfully  completed  similar  projects  in  the  cities  of
Cerritos,  Lakewood,  and Solvang.

The SCADA  Project  is planned  to begin  May  2024 and be completed  by July 2025.

The proposed  Agreement  is pursuant  to an RFP process.  On March  23, 2023,  an RFP  for the
SCADA  Project  was released  to five  qualified  consulting  firins.  On May  8, 2023,  two proposals
were  received  in the City  Clerk's  Office,  one from  HydroScientific  West  and one from  Macro
Automatics.  A technical  panel  comprised  of the City's  Water  Division  Manager,  Long  Beach
Water  Department  Manager  of Engineering,  and the Project  Manager  evaluated  the consultants.
The  review  criteria  weighed  a number  of  factors  including  fees,  project  manager  and team
qualifications,  experience  in  similar  projects,  understanding  of  technical  issues,
comprehensiveness  of the proposal,  and experience  in SCADA  projects.  Based on the evaluation,
HydroScientific  West received  the highest  ranking.  The primary  reason  for receiving  the highest
ranking  was the company  designed  and installed  the existing  SCADA  system  which  offered  value
in upgrading  the existing  system.  The company  was awarded  a contract  but was unable  to perform
the project  for extraordinary  circumstances.  As such, staff is recommending  awarding  the contract
to the second highest  ranked  consultant,  Macro  Automatics.

   City of South Gate SCADA System Upgrade Technical Description

I  Overview

The City of South Gate operates a water SCADA system that uses an outdated Human Machine Interface
(HMI) and Programmable  Logic Controller (PLC) platform. This proposal describes the work and cost to
upgrade the HMI and PLCs with up-to-date and supported replacements.

The existing Control Microsystems  PLCs are outdated.  Some of these PLCs use the ISAGraph programming
software that is no longer supported and others use the Telepace programming  software designed in the
1990s. The Control Microsystems  PLCs will be replaced with Schneider Modicon M251 PLCs. The M25ls will
be programmed  in standard IEC 61131-3 languages supported by many modern PLCs. The M251 supports
Modbus protocol for compatibility  with existing equipment,  EtherNeUIP forAllen Bradley connectivity, and OPC-
LIA for secure connections  to the HMI.

The ClearSCADA  HMI will be replaced with Inductive Automation's Ignition HMI. Ignition is an enterprise-
grade HMI platform widely supported system integrators.  There are dozens of certified Ignition integrators  in
Southern California.

2 Scope  of Work

Work will be conducted at the City Yard control room and off-site facilities.  All functionality of the existing
SCADA system will be ported to the new system along with improvements  in graphics, alarm call-out, trending,
reporting, and communications.

Generally, the work at each remote will involve replacing the mounting panels at each remote site with new
mounting panels that have been pre-wired and tested. The field wiring will be reconnected  to the new
mounting panel terminal blocks. Some site will require additional work to accommodate  new or relocated field
sensors and actuators.

The City will furnish  Verizon  wireless  cellular  service/SIM  card for the cellular  modem  used to send SMS
alarms.

  PURPOSE:  To  accept  the construction  of the East Alameda  Street  Sidewalk  Improvements
  Project,  City  Project  No.  660-ST  ("Project")  as completed.  Construction  of  the  Project  is
  completed  and  the  retention  payment  to the  contractor  is due.  Section  7107  of  the  Public
  Contract  Code  requires  the City  to accept  completion  of the Project  and issue public  notice  of
  such, prior  to releasing  the retention  payment.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Accepting  completion  of  construction  of  the  East  Alameda  Street  Sidewalk
  Improvements  Project,  City  Project  No.  660-ST  by  Sequel  Contractors,  Inc.,  effective
  Apn1 Q, 2024;  anrl
  b.  Directing  the  City  Clerk  to  file  a Notice  of  Completion  with  Los  Angeles  County
  Registrar  Recorder's  Office.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact  to the General  Fund.  The final  construction  cost
  was $963,581,  inclusive  of contract  change  orders,  and funded  as sui'nunarized  below.

  ANALYSIS:  Construction  of the Project  is complete  and staff  is preparing  to release  the final
  retention  payment  to Seqriel  Contractors,  Inc. The Public  Contract  Code establishes  requirements
  that the City  must  abide  to prior  to releasing  the final  retention  payment  for  the Project.  The
  Notice  of Completion  provides  written  notice  to concerned  parties  that  all work  on the project
  has  been  completed.  The  Notice  of  Completion  initiates  the  35-day  period  within  which

City  may  use a part or all of the 5% retention  payment  to settle  any liens  exercised  against  the

BACKGROUND:  The  Project  is part  of  the  Fiscal  Year  2022/23  Capital  Improvement
Program.  The  Project  will  improve  pedestrian  safety  and  enhance  access  to  Simon  Rodia
Continuation  High  School  located  on  Sequoia  Drive,  east of  East  Alameda  Street.  Project
improvements  entail  the construction  of new sidewalks  on the east side of East Alameda  Street,
from  Sequoia  Drive  to Seminole  Avenue,  and on the south  side of Sequoia  Drive,  from  East
Alameda  Street to the east cul-de-sac.  The work  included  the reconstruction  of curb and gutters,
reconstruction  of drive  approaches,  construction  of new  sidewalks,  removal  and replanting  of
trees, relocation  of streetlights,  relocation  of fire hydrants,  and the reconstruction  of rolling  gates
and wrought  iron fences.

On January  24, 2023,  the City  Council  awarded  the construction  of the Project  in the amount  of
$903,361.  Construction  began  on April  5, 2023,  and was field  accepted  by City  staff on October
19, 2023. All  work  was perfon'ned  in accordance  with  the approved  plans and specifications  with
acceptable  quality  and workmanship.  The Contractor  has met all contract  obligations.

Five  change  orders  were needed  to complete  construction  for a total  of $60,220.  Change  Order
No. 1 was at no cost to the City  and provided  a 30-day  schedule  extension.  Change  Order  No. 2,
in the amount  of $20,682,  was for installing  conduit,  conductors,  and pull  boxes.  Change  Order
No.  3, in the amount  of $4,057, was to modify  an existing  fire  detector  check  valve.  Change
Order  No.  5, in the amount  of $4,444,  was for the removal  of existing  pilasters.  Change  Order
No. 6, in-the  amount-of  $31-,037, was-for  fire hydran-t  upgrades  needed to cornpl-ete  constructi

It is noted  that Change  No. 4 was not processed  thus not listed.  It is also noted  that construction
completion  was  accepted  on October  19,  2023.  Approval  of the Notice  of Completion  was
delayed  because  of pending  change  order negotiations  which  were finalized  in December  2023.

The City  Council  may now  accept  the Project  as complete.  The Notice  of Completion  can now
be filed  with  the Los Angeles  County  Registrar  Recorder's  Office

 SUBJECT:  CONSID  ADOPTION  OF RESOLUTION  MAKING  CERT AIN FINDINGS
 FOR AN EXCEPTION  TO THE 180-DAY  WAIT  PERIOD  PURSUANT  TO CALIFORNIA
 GOVERNMENT  CODE  SECTIONS  7522.56 AND 21221

 PURPOSE:  The Pension Reform Act of 2012 prohibits employers from hiring retired annuitants
 within 180 days of their retirement. However, subsequent legislation provides for an exception to the
 180-day wait period under specific conditions, i.e., the California Public Employees' Retirement
 System (CalPERS) requires the City Council adopt a resolution to allow for an exception to the 180-
 day wait period to hire a retired employee for temporary, part-time employment during the wait period.

 RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City Council is requested to consider adoption of a Resolution
 making certain findings that allow a retired Police Captain-In-Charge to be hired for temporary, part-
 time employment commencing within the 180-day wait period from his retirement from the City of
 South  Gate.

 FISCAL IMPACT:  The making of certain findings for an exception to the 180-day wait period will
 require no additional appropriations for Fiscal Year 2023/24 due to salary savings from the Senior
 Administrative  Analyst and the Intermediate Account Clerk positions being vacant in the Police
 Department will be used to cover the salary cost for the returning retired annuitant.

 ANALYSIS:  None.

 BACKGROUND:  Police Captain-In-Charge  James "Jim" Teeples ("Capt. Teeples") retired from the
 Police Department effective December 2, 2023, after a 28-year career with the City of South Gate.
 Capt. Teeples was initially hired by the City on September 24, 1995, as a Police Officer and worked
 his way up the ranks, being promoted to Captain-In-Charge  on November  7, 2021.

 In addition to Capt. Teeples' ordinary duties as a police captain overseeing certain policing operations
 and functions, he also had substantial duties related to the effective administration  of a police
 department, such as persoru'iel, supervision of non-sworn staff, and budgeting. Specifically,  he
 supervised the Senior Administrative  Analyst (Police), whose duties included budget preparation,
 fiscal controls, monitoring capital improvements, conducting job applicant screening  and processing,
 attending hiring and recruitment events, tending certain community-based  programs,  and assisting in
 special projects as assigned by the Chief of Police. However, along with Capt. Teeples' retirement  at

  l

  315
 the end of last year,  so, too, did the pervious  Senior  Administrative  Analyst  decide  to retire,  who had
31 years with  the Police  Department.

The  retired  Senior  Administrative  Analyst  provided  ample  notice  to  the  City  of  her  impending
retirement  and the City  initiated  a comprehensive  recruitment  for her replacement  on September  20,
2023,  which  yielded  two promising  candidates,  both  of which  withdrew  later during  the process.  As a
result,  the City  has been actively  recruiting  for this position  but has yet to fill  it. However,  the Police
Department  had  a capable  Inten'nediate  Account  Clerk  who  picked  up many  of the budget-related
duties  the  Sei'iior  Administrative  Analyst  performed  and was  providing  a tremendous  amount  of
assistance  to the Police  Department  in relation  to the budgetary  process.  However,  the Inteimediate
Account  Clerk  resigned  from  her position  for an opportunity  with  another  employer  on February  29,
2024.

As  a result  of the loss of three  key  personnel  due to retirement  and resignation  since  December  2,
2023, who have been integral  in the Police  Department's  budget  preparation  process,  it is necessary  to
have Capt. Teeples  return  to perfornn  special  projects  and work  related  to this budgetary  process,  which
includes  working  with  the Administrative  Services  Department  in analyzing  the budget  needs  of the
department,  coordinating  with  purchasing  in  the  acquisition  of  equipment,  handling  the  Asset
Forfeiture  Program  expenditures  for  the  police  department,  and  a number  of  key  duties  in  the
performance  of budget  preparation  and management  of Police  Department  funds.

Pursuant to California Governi'nent  Code F>7522.56(b), "[a] retired person shall not serve, be employed
by,  or be employed  through  a contract  directly  by a public  employer  in the same public  retirement
system  from  which  the retiree  received  the benefit  without  reinstatement  from  retirement,  except  as
permitted  by this  section."  California  Government  Code  F§ 7522.56(c),  then  provides  the following
exception:  "A  retired  person  may  serve  without  reinstatement  or loss  or interniption  of  benefits
provided  by [CalPERS]  upon  appointment  by the appointing  power  of a public  employer  either  during
an emergency  to prevent  stoppage  of public  business  or because  the retired  person  has specialized
skills needed in performing work of a limited duration." California Government Code E>7522.56(f)(1)
provides:  "A  retired  person  shall not be eligible  to be employed  pursuant  to this section  for a period  of
180  days  following  the  date  of  retirement  unless...  [t]he  employer  certifies  the  nature  of  the
employment  and the appointment  is necessary  to fill  a critically  needed  position  before  180 days have
passed  and the appointment  has been  approved  by the governing  body  of the employer  in a public
meeting.  The appointment  may not be placed  on the consent  calendar."  The City  is currently  recruiting
to  fill  the  Senior  Administrative  Analyst  vacancy;  however,  Capt.  Teeples  specialized  skills  are
critically  needed  to prepare  the budget  in time  for the next fiscal  year and before  180 days have passed
since his retirement  from  the City  of South  Gate.  His  28-year  depth  of knowledge  and his personal
contacts  with  all public  agency  and private  entity  stakeholders  are vital  and essential  to the continued
success  of the City's  Police  Department.  Additionally,  Capt.  Teeples  has not  accepted  a retirement
incentive  upon  his retirement,  which  would  make  him  ineligible  for this  consideration  as outlined  in
California  Governrnent  Code §7522.56(g).

Capt. Teeples  employment  will  be on a temporary,  part-time  basis and will  remain  at or below  the 960
permitted  hours  per fiscal  year a retired  annuitant  may  work  pursuant  to California  Government  Code
§ 7522.56(d).  His specialized  skills  are needed  to ensure  there is no backlog  of work  as the budgetary
process  is completed  and that  any current  special  projects  to which  he can be assigned  remain  on
schedule  and without  interniption.  Once  the City  has hired  a permanent  incumbent  to fill  the vacant
Senior  Administrative  Analyst  position  and Capt. Teeples  has been able to pass along  any skills  and/or

  2

  316
 knowledge  necessary  to transition  all his duties  to the new  employee,  his  employment  as a retired
annuitant  will  no longer  be necessary.  It is anticipated  that this process  will  last the duration  of the
current  fiscal  year and continue  into the 2024-2025  fiscal  year.

Also, pursuant to California  Government Code F>7522.56(d), Capt. Teeples  pay may  not exceed  the
maximum  monthly  base salary  paid  to other  employees  perforining  comparable  duties  as listed  on a
publicly  available  pay  schedule  equal  to the hourly  rate.  The  maximum  base salaiy  for  the Senior
Administrative  Analyst  is $8,947,  and the hourly  equivalent  is $51.62.  Therefore,  Capt. Teeples  will  be
paid at the rate of $51.62/hour  for duties  performed  as a retired  annuitant  in the capacity  of the Senior
Administrative  Analyst.

Accordingly,  staff  recommends  the City  Council  adopt  a Resolution  making  certain  findings  for  an
exception  to the 180-day  wait period  pursuant  to California  Government  Code §§ 7522.56  & 21221.
